basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 21.' and it opens 'Vers. 21. De Sem quoque nati sunt, quos nunc dicemus, qui fuit pater omnium filiorum'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 21. De Sem quoque nati sunt, quos nunc dicemus, qui fuit pater omnium filiorum Heber, et frater major minoris fratris Japheth. Ideo autem de hoc novissime locutus est, quia de istius generatione locuturus erat et hujus lineam prosecuturus.
